citation.title: Patient Subtyping via Time-Aware LSTM Networks
citation.authors: Inci M. Baytas; Cao Xiao; Xi Zhang; Fei Wang; Anil K. Jain; Jiayu Zhou
citation.venue: Proceedings of KDD 2017 (ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining)

topic: An LSTM variant that discounts a learned short-term memory component by a decay function of the elapsed time between irregularly spaced records. It is applied to clustering of EHR and PPMI patient sequences.
own_question: Can modelling the elapsed time inside the memory cell improve representations of irregularly sampled patient records for classification, target-sequence prediction and subtyping?
actual_method_and_evidence: T-LSTM, defined in equations on pp.4-5, decays the short-term memory by g(Δt), for example 1/log(e+Δt). The source authors report three results. On synthetic EHR data, T-LSTM had a mean AUC of 0.91 (Table 1). On a synthetic clustering task, the mean Rand index was 0.96 (Table 2). On PPMI target prediction, the mean MSE was 0.50 versus 0.51 for LSTM (Table 4), a small difference within the reported standard deviations. The evidence comes from healthcare data only, with no plasma data and no timing or latency measurements.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are past records together with the elapsed gaps between them. The model performs offline sequence modelling and does not address real-time causal nowcasting of a currently pending report.
validation_if_relevant: Validation used repeated random 70/30 splits, with no held-out campaign. This does not map onto our four validation designs.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim irregular-interval RNNs have been validated for CES or fusion diagnostics.
Do not imply that T-LSTM is part of our method or one of our baselines.
Do not cite the small PPMI MSE gap as evidence that time-aware models generally improve accuracy.
Do not equate EHR visit gaps with CES report latency.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional at most, as one example in a background sentence noting that gated recurrent models can take elapsed-time gaps as an input. It is not needed for our framing, our baselines or our evidence, and adds nothing physics-specific.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
